note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in PA.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: The Great Lakes Seaway Trail
byways.where: PA 5 and Alternate PA 5 from US 20 to the New York line, with the Bayfront Parkway and Peninsula Drive, Erie County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Seaway Trail (effective 2003) as PA Route 5 and Alternate Route 5 from the US 20/PA 5 junction to the New York line, including the Bayfront Parkway and Peninsula Drive.
PA 5 parallels Lake Erie through Erie County and at Lake City runs only about 2,000 feet south of the lake.
The Pennsylvania section gives access to Presque Isle State Park, the Presque Isle Lighthouse, the Erie Maritime Museum and the USS Niagara.

byways.name: The Lake Wilhelm
byways.where: SR 1019 (Creek Road) to PA 173, Mercer County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Lake Wilhelm byway (effective 2006) on S.R. 1019, Creek Road, ending at S.R. 173 in Mercer County.
The byway runs along Creek Road through part of Maurice K. Goddard State Park, whose 1,680-acre Lake Wilhelm is popular with anglers and boaters.

byways.review: PennDOT calls it 'The Lake Wilhelm'; Visit PA uses Lake Wilhelm Scenic Byway.

byways.name: Crawford Lakelands Byway
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 68 of 2011)
byways.where: US 6/322, PA 18, PA 618, PA 285 and SR 3011 between Jamestown and Linesville, Crawford County

facts.fact: The byway uses US 6 from the Ohio line, PA 18, PA 618, PA 285 and S.R. 3011 through Conneaut Lake, Linesville and nearby townships, under SB 606, Act 68 of 2011.
Designated in 2011, it runs from Jamestown to Linesville on PA 285, PA 618, PA 18 and US 6.
Conneaut Lake is Pennsylvania's largest natural lake, and at the Pymatuning Spillway ducks walk on dense schools of fish.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. PennDOT RMS segments flagged as byway in Crawford County are exactly US 6, PA 18, PA 285, PA 618 and SR 3011.

byways.name: The Kinzua
byways.where: SR 3011 from US 6 to Kinzua Bridge State Park, McKean County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Kinzua byway (effective 2001) as Route 3011, connecting Route 6 with Kinzua Bridge in McKean County.
Kinzua was the first byway designated under PennDOT's 2001 program.
Kinzua Bridge State Park has a skywalk built on six of the viaduct's steel towers that remained after a 2003 tornado, overlooking the Kinzua Gorge.

byways.review: Catalog name Kinzua Bridge Byway; PennDOT lists 'The Kinzua'.

byways.name: High Plateau
byways.where: PA 144 between Snow Shoe (I-80 exit 147) and Renovo, Centre and Clinton counties

facts.fact: PennDOT lists High Plateau (effective 2002) as S.R. 144 in Sproul State Forest, Clinton and Centre counties.
The 27-mile corridor between Snow Shoe and Renovo runs on top of the Allegheny plateau with no power lines or homes in view.
The Dennison Overlook near State Camp, at about 2,200 feet, is listed in the Dark Skies Directory.

byways.name: Bucktail Trail
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 33 of 2003)
byways.where: PA 120 from Lock Haven to US 219 at Ridgway, Clinton, Cameron and Elk counties

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Bucktail Trail (effective January 6, 2004) as S.R. 120 from Lock Haven through Cameron County to US 219 in Elk County, under HB 1549, Act 33 of 2003.

Route 120 is named for a Civil War era regiment of rangers and runs about 100 miles through Sproul and Elk state forests from Lock Haven to Renovo, along the West Branch Susquehanna, and on to Ridgway via Emporium and St. Marys.

byways.name: West Branch Susquehanna River Byway
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 63 of 2011)
byways.where: US 219, US 322, PA 153, 453, 729, 879, 969, SR 1001, SR 4005 and Bilger's Rocks Road between Karthaus and Cherry Tree, Clearfield County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the byway (effective July 7, 2011, SB 369, Act 63 of 2011) on US 219, US 322, PA 969, 879, 153, 453, 729, SR 1001, SR 4005, the Greenville Pike and Bilger's Rocks Road in Clearfield County.
The 72-mile byway between Karthaus and Cherry Tree largely follows the river on 11 routes, passing McGee's Mills Covered Bridge, Bilger's Rocks and Curwensville Lake, with elk among its wildlife.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. Omitted from the Wikipedia list.

byways.name: Governor Casey Byway
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 33 of 2003)
byways.where: US 6 from I-81 in Dunmore to Business US 6 in Carbondale Township, Lackawanna County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Governor Casey Byway (effective January 6, 2004) as US 6 between I-81 in Dunmore and Business Route 6 in Carbondale Township, under HB 1549, Act 33 of 2003.
The byway gives access to Steamtown National Historic Site, the Pennsylvania Anthracite Heritage Museum and the Lackawanna Coal Mine.

byways.review: Visit PA and Wikipedia end it at PA 247 in Jessup; PennDOT RW-745 runs it on to Business 6 in Carbondale Township.

byways.name: Gateway to the Endless Mountains
byways.where: Business US 6 through Tunkhannock, Wyoming County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the byway (effective September 5, 2005) on Business Route 6 between its interchanges west and east of Tunkhannock Borough; off-premise signs are prohibited by SB 721, Act 35 of 2005.
The byway runs along US 6 in Tunkhannock, Wyoming County, in the Endless Mountains region, and passes the Dietrich Theatre.

byways.review: Shortest rural PA byway, about 3.6 miles.

byways.name: Viaduct Valley Way
byways.where: PA 92 with PA 171 and local routes between Dixon and Lanesboro, Wyoming and Susquehanna counties

facts.fact: PennDOT lists Viaduct Valley Way in three designations (2005, 2007, 2012) on PA 92, PA 171 and SRs 1009 and 1015 from Dixon to Lanesboro.

The 37.3-mile byway runs through valley farmland and bluestone quarry country and passes the Starrucca Viaduct, the oldest stone railroad bridge still in use in Pennsylvania, and the concrete Tunkhannock Creek Viaduct.
The byway passes under the Tunkhannock Viaduct.

byways.review: Visit PA names PA 171, 92 and 11; PennDOT names PA 92, 171, SR 1009 and SR 1015.

byways.name: Delaware River Valley Scenic Byway
byways.where: PA 611, Little Creek Road and Belvidere Highway from Easton to Riverton, Northampton County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the byway (effective 2005) on Route 611, Little Creek Road and Belvidere Highway in Northampton County.
It winds 17 miles through farmland between Easton and Riverton, past riverside towns, with the Delaware River and Little Martin's Creek as backdrop.

byways.name: Blue Route
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 58 of 1993)
byways.where: I-476 from I-95 near Chester to the Pennsylvania Turnpike at Plymouth Meeting, Delaware and Montgomery counties

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Blue Route (effective July 2, 1993, HB 986, Act 58) on I-476 from the I-95 interchange in Delaware County to the I-276 interchange in Montgomery County.
The 20-mile Mid-County Expressway took its nickname from a 1958 location report whose map drew the alternatives in colors; the blue route through the Crum Creek valley was chosen.
The byway gives access to Ridley Creek State Park and Tyler Arboretum.

byways.review: An interstate designated by the legislature; PennDOT treats it as a legislative scenic byway (billboard ban).

byways.name: Exton Bypass
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 82 of 1996)
byways.where: US 30 bypass from US 202 west to near Bell Tavern Road, Chester County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Exton Bypass (effective July 2, 1996, HB 2336, Act 82) as the middle portion of the US 30 bypass from the US 202 interchange to about 500 feet west of the Bell Tavern Road overpass.
The Exton Bypass was completed in December 1995, joining the Coatesville Downingtown Bypass to give US 30 a continuous freeway from PA 10 to US 202.
The byway lies near the historic Lincoln Highway and the American Helicopter Museum.

byways.review: No working official page; the National Scenic Byway Foundation page (nsbfoundation.com/sb/exton-bypass-scenic-byway/) refuses automated fetches.

byways.name: Brandywine Valley Scenic Byway
byways.where: PA 52, PA 162 and Old Creek Road (old PA 100), Chester and Delaware counties

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Brandywine Valley Scenic Byway (effective 2005) on Route 52, Route 162 and Old Creek Road (old PA Route 100).
FHWA lists it as a 25.26-mile National Scenic Byway in Pennsylvania and Delaware, through a valley of commerce, agriculture and art, with structures tied to the Underground Railroad along the way.
The byway gives access to Longwood Gardens and the Brandywine River Museum.

byways.review: Catalog lists it only as a state byway; FHWA now lists it as a National Scenic Byway (PA and DE).

byways.name: U.S. Route 202 Parkway
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 140 of 2012)
byways.where: US 202 parkway from PA 63 (Welsh Road), Montgomery County, to PA 611 in Doylestown Township, Bucks County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the US 202 Parkway (effective September 5, 2012, SB 1551, Act 140 of 2012) between PA 63 in Montgomery County and PA 611 in Doylestown Township, Bucks County.
The parkway opened on December 3, 2012; it has landscaping and split-rail fences, bans billboards, and is paralleled by the US 202 Parkway Trail through fields and woods.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. No working official page; the National Scenic Byway Foundation page refuses automated fetches and gives figures for all of US 202.

byways.name: Lebanon Cornwall Byway
byways.where: PA 419 from PA 72 at Quentin to the Berks County line, Lebanon County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Lebanon Cornwall Byway (effective 2008) on Route 419 from its intersection with PA 72 at Quentin to the Berks County line.
The byway passes farmland and Amish communities, with stops at the Cornwall Iron Furnace and the Middle Creek wildlife area.
It runs between Cornwall and Newmanstown.

byways.review: Catalog calls it Route 419 Scenic Byway; rename to Lebanon Cornwall Byway.

byways.name: Journey Through Hallowed Ground
byways.where: US 15 and Business US 15 from the Maryland line through Gettysburg, Adams County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Pennsylvania section (effective 2009) from Business 15 at the Cumberland Township line through Gettysburg and Freedom Township to US 15 at the Maryland line.
The U.S. Secretary of Transportation designated the 180-mile route as a National Scenic Byway on October 16, 2009.
The national byway runs from Gettysburg to Monticello in Virginia.

byways.name: Conestoga Ridge Byway
byways.where: PA 23 from US 322 at Blue Ball to PA 10 west of Morgantown, Lancaster County

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the Conestoga Ridge Byway (effective 2013) on PA 23 between Route 10 and Route 322 in Caernarvon and East Earl townships, Lancaster County.
It runs between US 322 in Blue Ball and PA 10 west of Morgantown, through farmland and the communities of Goodville and Churchtown.
The byway follows a ridge above the Conestoga River valley, among small Amish and Mennonite farms bordered by wooded hillsides.

byways.name: The National Road
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 115 of 1996); All-American Road
byways.where: US 40 from the Maryland line to the West Virginia line, Somerset, Fayette and Washington counties

facts.fact: PennDOT lists the National Road (effective September 11, 1996, HB 1712, Act 115) as S.R. 40 from the Maryland border to the West Virginia border.
Southeast of Uniontown US 40 passes the Historic Summit Inn and Fort Necessity National Battlefield; to the west it crosses the Monongahela near Brownsville on the Lane Bane Bridge.
The road was the nation's first federally funded interstate highway, lined today with inns, tollhouses and diners.

byways.name: Grand View
byways.where: Grandview Avenue, P.J. McArdle Roadway and Sycamore Street, Mount Washington, Pittsburgh

facts.fact: PennDOT lists Grand View (effective 2003) as Grandview Avenue, McArdle Roadway and Sycamore Street in Pittsburgh.
The byway looks over downtown Pittsburgh and gives access to the Monongahela Incline, the Duquesne Incline and the Mount Washington overlook.

byways.name: Laurel Highlands
byways.designation: Pennsylvania Byway (legislative scenic byway, Act 115 of 1996)
byways.where: PA 711 from the Conemaugh River (Seward) to Normalville, then PA 381 to the West Virginia line, Westmoreland and Fayette counties

facts.fact: PennDOT lists Laurel Highlands (effective September 11, 1996) as PA 711 from the Conemaugh River to Jones Mills, Routes 711/381 to Normalville, and PA 381 to the West Virginia line.
The 68-mile byway along Routes 711 and 381 passes Frank Lloyd Wright buildings and offers rafting and tubing on the way.
It gives access to Ohiopyle State Park, Fallingwater, Kentuck Knob and Fort Ligonier.

byways.name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Byway
byways.where: PA 52 and nearby roads from the Delaware line into Chester County

facts.fact: PennDOT designated the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Byway as Pennsylvania's 23rd byway in November 2022, extending the Maryland and Delaware Tubman byways; it was designated for its historic qualities.
The Delaware byway reaches the Pennsylvania line on Route 52, where the Pennsylvania byway begins; it is managed by the Brandywine Valley Scenic Byway Commission.
The byway follows the backroads of Chester County and tells of Quaker and African American abolitionists and free Black communities and their churches.

byways.review: Not in the catalog and not in PennDOT's 2023 RW-745 list. Its line largely shares PA 52 with the Brandywine Valley byway plus a stretch of US 1 (Baltimore Pike), so PennDOT's segment flags cannot isolate it. A non-agency ArcGIS Online layer (see gis.notes) draws it as Byway='Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Byway'.

byways.name: Pennsylvania Route 6 Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 6 across Warren, McKean, Potter and Tioga counties

facts.fact: PA Route 6 was designated as Pennsylvania's 24th and longest scenic byway, 211 miles across Warren, McKean, Potter and Tioga counties, celebrated October 30, 2025 in Coudersport after all 34 municipalities passed resolutions.
The corridor connects the Allegheny National Forest, the Kinzua Bridge Skywalk, the Pennsylvania Grand Canyon and 22 state parks, and includes extensions and offsets of US 6.
Between Coudersport and Ansonia US 6 follows Pine Creek through Galeton, near the head of the Pine Creek Gorge.

byways.review: Not in the catalog; designated October 2025. paroute6.com refuses curl but loads in a browser and through WebFetch. The four-county RMS flags (about 187 miles) cover US 6 end to end in those counties; the published 211 miles includes extensions and offsets that are not flagged.

byways.name: Longhouse National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Loop on PA 321, PA 59 and Longhouse Drive (FR 262) around the Kinzua Creek arm of the Allegheny Reservoir, Warren and McKean counties

facts.fact: The Longhouse Scenic Byway is a 36-mile loop through the Allegheny National Forest's northern hardwoods of oak and black cherry, circling the Kinzua Creek arm of the Allegheny Reservoir.
The loop starts at Route 321 and Longhouse Drive, follows Route 59 past the Rimrock Overlook to the reservoir, crosses Cornplanter Bridge and returns on Longhouse Drive near Jakes Rocks Overlook.

byways.review: PennDOT's program page counts this as its 'one Forestry Byway'; it is listed separately because the Forest Service designated it.

issues: PennDOT's program page says 21 PA Byways, one Forestry Byway and four National Scenic Byways but lists none. RW-745ISB (7-23) lists 21 named byways including the four national ones; the Tubman byway (Nov 2022, 'PA's 23rd') is missing from it, and US 6 (Oct 2025, 'PA's 24th') came later. This chapter lists 23 PennDOT byways plus Longhouse = 24, matching the 24-feature ArcGIS layer and Scenic America's count.
Six state byways are not in the catalog: Crawford Lakelands, West Branch Susquehanna River, US 202 Parkway, Conestoga Ridge, Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Byway and PA Route 6.
Catalog route-419-scenic-byway-76816 is PennDOT's Lebanon Cornwall Byway (PA 419, Quentin to the Berks line); its bbox fits. Rename.
Catalog brandywine-valley-scenic-byway-64115 lists only 'Pennsylvania State Scenic Byway', but FHWA lists Brandywine Valley Scenic Byway (id 64115) as a National Scenic Byway in PA and DE.

Governor Casey extent disagrees: RW-745 says I-81 Dunmore to Business 6 in Carbondale Township; Visit PA and Wikipedia say to PA 247 in Jessup. Catalog bbox reaches about 41.577 N, consistent with the longer PennDOT extent.
Viaduct Valley Way routes disagree: Visit PA says PA 171, 92 and 11; PennDOT says PA 92, 171, SR 1009 and SR 1015.
Seaway Trail start: RW-745 starts at the US 20/PA 5 junction, but Wikipedia and PennDOT RMS flags (US 20 segs 0010-0031) include US 20 from the Ohio line.
Exton Bypass and US 202 Parkway have no working official page (nsbfoundation.com pages return 403; its 202 page describes all of US 202, 59 miles).
Blurbs for Conestoga Ridge cite the non-agency ArcGIS layer's About field for the Amish and Mennonite farms and the Conestoga valley.
The Visit PA statewide byways trip page is 'being updated' and shows only two byways; individual Visit PA listing pages (www.visitpa.com/listing/<slug>/<id>/) work.
